claims.text: Reopening the House of Councillors Committee on Rules and Administration at 11:58, the Secretary General (佐伯英明) reports that at 09:45 that day the House received a notice from Prime Minister Kaifu (海部内閣総理大臣), addressed to the President of the House, that the Cabinet had decided that day to resign en masse (総辞職).

locator.item: 内閣総辞職に関する報告

claims.uncertainty: Records the Cabinet's decision to resign en masse, as notified, on the day the 118th (special) session convened after the 18 February 1990 general election; the committee had recessed at 09:45, so the time belongs to the receipt only. It is not an end of Kaifu's office: no source reviewed states the day his first appointment ended, and none states that he continued to perform the duties until a successor was appointed. The same notice is not recorded in the House of Representatives' minutes of that day. The clock time is not stored.

claims.text: Speaker Doi reports to the House that on that day she received from Prime Minister Hosokawa (細川内閣総理大臣) a written notice that the cabinet had decided to resign en masse; the House then proceeds to the designation.
claims.uncertainty: Only the surname is printed (細川内閣総理大臣). A notice or record of the Cabinet's decision to resign en masse (総辞職) is not the end of the Prime Minister's office. Constitution art. 71 (procedure only) keeps the outgoing Cabinet performing its functions until a new Prime Minister is appointed, but no source reviewed states that the outgoing Prime Minister did so, and no end is dated from it.

claims.text: Recorded ballot for the designation: 502 votes cast, majority 252; 羽田孜 274, 河野洋平 207, 不破哲三 15, 6 invalid (no name). The Speaker declares that the House designates 羽田孜 as Prime Minister under HR Rules art. 18(2).
claims.uncertainty: A Diet designation is not the appointment; never a start.

claims.text: The record headed 小渕内閣総理大臣記者会見録, 31 July 1998, has 小渕総理 open by saying he has come to bear the heavy responsibility of Prime Minister and later that 'today' he has come to bear responsibility as Prime Minister (本日、私がこうして総理としての責任を負うことになりました).

locator.part: 冒頭発言 paragraph 1; 質疑応答 answer on the United States

claims.uncertainty: Same-day in-office attestation; it states no day of appointment. Its spoken 本日…総理としての責任を負うことになりました is not read as an assumption statement: it is an oral answer, and the same record's opening remarks say the new cabinet was launched the previous day. The written 本日…重責を担う statements accepted as starts elsewhere (for example 11 January 1996) are dated statements issued in writing on the day and name no other day.

claims.text: In the same opening remarks 小渕総理 says the new cabinet was launched the previous day (まずは昨日新しい内閣が発足することができた).

locator.heading: 小渕内閣総理大臣記者会見録

claims.uncertainty: Next-day statement by the holder about the cabinet's launch, dated by the day it recalls (30 July): a claim, not a start; it does not speak of his own appointment ceremony.

claims.text: Aoki told the House that Prime Minister Obuchi (小渕総理) had been admitted to Juntendo Hospital about 01:00 on 2 April 2000 for overwork, that before 21:00 that day he was told that Obuchi had been moved to intensive care, and that Obuchi fell into a coma about 23:30.

locator.speaker: 青木幹雄 (内閣官房長官)
locator.part: paragraphs on 2 April (02:00 report, 21:00 intensive care, 23:30 coma)

claims.uncertainty: Retrospective account given on 10 April by the acting prime minister himself; dated by the day it describes. Obuchi is printed as 小渕総理 / 小渕前総理 (surname only). It states no end of his office.

claims.text: Aoki told the House that when he saw Prime Minister Obuchi (小渕総理) at the hospital about 19:00 on 2 April 2000, Obuchi, mindful of the Usu volcano, instructed him to take care of everything if anything happened (何かあれば万事よろしく頼む), and that before the 23:30 press conference he told 宮澤 that he would serve as acting prime minister (臨時代理) as needed under that instruction.

locator.part: paragraph beginning 午後六時ごろ, and the paragraph on the telephone call to 宮澤大蔵大臣

claims.uncertainty: Acting service (臨時代理) is a claim only and never a holder; the row carries no holder name. The government's answer of 23 May 2000 reads this instruction as including the instruction to serve as acting prime minister under Cabinet Act art. 9; that reading is the government's, recorded in jp_sangiin_homu_20000523_matsutani, and it sets no start of acting service.

claims.text: Aoki (青木幹雄) stated that at the regular 11:00 press conference on 3 April 2000 he announced that, weighing the Usu volcano response and other urgent matters, he had accepted the acting prime ministership (臨時代理) at 09:00.
claims.uncertainty: Acting service (臨時代理) is a claim only and never a holder; the row carries no holder name. Retrospective account of 10 April 2000 dated by the day it describes; the acting designation's notice is a separate claim (jp_aoki_reports_acting_designation_notified_20000403).

claims.text: Aoki (青木幹雄) stated that at the 12:40 extraordinary cabinet meeting on 3 April 2000 he reported the Prime Minister's condition and the acting designation (臨時代理指定), notified the Speakers of both Houses and had it published in the Official Gazette (官報公告).

locator.part: paragraph beginning また、同日午後十二時四十分の臨時閣議で

claims.uncertainty: Acting service (臨時代理) is a claim only and never a holder; the row carries no holder name. The Gazette notice he mentions was not accessible (the Official Gazette for 2000 is not available without restriction).

claims.text: Aoki stated that after hearing the doctors at 14:30 on 4 April 2000 he judged Prime Minister Obuchi's (小渕総理) condition to be a case where the Prime Minister is 'lacking' (欠けたとき) under Constitution art. 70, and that an extraordinary cabinet meeting at 19:00 that day decided the cabinet's resignation en masse.
claims.uncertainty: The art. 70 judgment is the cabinet's own; the constitutional reading is procedure only. No source states the day Obuchi's office ended, and this packet sets no end for him.

locator.speaker: 堀川久士 (参議院事務総長)

claims.uncertainty: Reported on 5 April about the previous day. The notice's signatory is the acting Prime Minister (青木内閣総理大臣臨時代理, surname only), so the row carries no holder name; it shows acting service on 4 April, a claim only. A notice or record of the Cabinet's decision to resign en masse (総辞職) is not the end of the Prime Minister's office. Constitution art. 71 (procedure only) keeps the outgoing Cabinet performing its functions until a new Prime Minister is appointed, but no source reviewed states that the outgoing Prime Minister did so, and no end is dated from it. claims.uncertainty: Dated by the Kantei's statement index (内閣総理大臣発言(H22.6.4)), the file name and the PDF's CreationDate; the text prints no date. The Chief Cabinet Secretary's press record of the same morning (jp_ccs_reports_hatoyama_final_cabinet_meeting_remarks_20100604) attributes the remarks to 鳩山総理 at the Hatoyama cabinet's last cabinet meeting. sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, emblems, seals, signatures, scanned pages or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: The Diet minutes API's JSON for the one speech record of the 衆議院 予算委員会 第17号 (2026-07-27), a transcription of the House's printed minutes; the exact API URL whose bytes were hashed is recorded, and the readable minutes page is https://kokkai.ndl.go.jp/txt/122105261X01720260727. The printed page images, served through a JavaScript viewer, were not viewed.

claims.text: The House of Representatives Budget Committee record No. 17 of 27 July 2026, a sitting held during the recess for an inquiry referred for 閉会中審査 (opened 09:01), lists among those attending 内閣総理大臣 高市早苗君.

locator.item: 会議録情報: the ministers listed as present after the 出席委員 list (below the dotted rule)

claims.uncertainty: An attestation of the holder in office on 27 July 2026. The National Diet Library files the record under the 221st session (第221回国会 予算委員会 第17号), but the sitting was held during the recess: the committee had on 24 July been referred 予算の実施状況に関する件 for 閉会中審査, the 221st special session having been fixed at 150 days to 17 July. A Diet search for her speeches from 1 June to 7 September 2026 found none later. It is neither a start nor an end.

sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, emblems, seals, signatures, scanned pages or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: A news article of the party's 2009 presidential election site (www.jimin.jp/sousai09/news/), recorded as a raw Internet Archive capture made before the cutoff. The same article at www.jimin.jp/jimin/daily/09_09/28/210928a.shtml has no capture.

claims.text: The party reports that the presidential election was counted on 28 September 2009 and 谷垣禎一候補 was chosen as the 24th LDP president with 300 votes (Diet-member votes 120, party-member votes 180); the Diet members voted from 14:00 at the eighth-floor hall of party headquarters; 河野太郎候補 received 144 (35, 109) and 西村康稔候補 54 (43, 11).

locator.section: date line 【平成２１年 ９月２８日】; headline; first paragraph

claims.uncertainty: A vote and count. Never a holder.

claims.text: About 40 minutes after the voting began, 野田毅総裁選挙管理委員長 announced the result together with the already counted party-member votes and declared 谷垣候補 elected (谷垣候補の当選を宣言).

locator.section: first paragraph, sentence beginning 投票開始から約４０分後

claims.uncertainty: The declaration of the result, kept apart from the vote and from any term start. Never a holder.

claims.text: At the joint plenary meeting in place of a party convention that followed (引き続き行われた「党大会に代わる両院議員総会」), 谷垣新総裁 gave an address pledging to lead the party's renewal and its return to government.

locator.section: first paragraph, sentence beginning 引き続き行われた

claims.uncertainty: Dates the holder observation of 28 September 2009; not a start, because no source states the day office took effect. Prints 谷垣新総裁 (surname and title); the article names 谷垣禎一 in full. The party's later list starts the term on 1 October 2009 and its schedule set 30 September 2009 as the day the previous term expired; the conflict is left unresolved.

claims.text: Afterwards 麻生太郎前総裁 and the two other candidates went up on the platform and shook hands with 谷垣新総裁.

locator.section: first paragraph, sentence beginning その後、麻生太郎前総裁

claims.uncertainty: It shows the party calling 麻生太郎 the former president on 28 September 2009 but states no day on which his presidency ended; it conflicts with the schedule's 30 September 2009 term expiry and the list's 30 September end. Never an until, and no end is inferred from the successor's election.

sources.publisher: Liberal Democratic Party of Japan (自由民主党, jimin.jp), via Internet Archive raw capture

sources.scope_note: A news article of the party's 2009 presidential election site (www.jimin.jp/sousai09/news/), recorded as a raw Internet Archive capture made before the cutoff.

claims.text: The party reports that 谷垣禎一新総裁, who had taken office as the party's 24th president (わが党第２４代総裁に就任した), held his first press conference as president (総裁として初めての記者会見) at party headquarters on the evening of 28 September 2009.

locator.section: date line 【平成２１年 ９月２８日】; headline 谷垣禎一総裁が初の記者会見; first paragraph

claims.uncertainty: Dates the holder observation of 28 September 2009; not a start, because no source states the day office took effect. 就任した says he had taken office by that evening but not the day it took effect; the party's own records conflict on that day (see the list and the 2009 schedule).

claims.text: The LDP's retrospective page 谷垣禎一総裁時代 (headed 平成21年10月1日～平成24年9月30日) says the party held a presidential election on 平成二十一年九月二十八日 (28 September 2009), in which 谷垣氏 won 300 votes (Diet-member votes 120, member-derived votes 180) against 河野氏 144 and 西村氏 54.

locator.section: heading; first and second paragraphs

claims.uncertainty: Retrospective party record written long after the event: a claim only, never a holder boundary; no structured date is stored. The election and its result only; the page's statements that 麻生総裁 had stepped down and that 谷垣氏 took office are separate claims.

claims.text: The same page says 谷垣氏 became the 24th LDP president (第二十四代自民党総裁に就任しました).

locator.section: second paragraph

claims.uncertainty: Retrospective party record written long after the event: a claim only, never a holder boundary; no structured date is stored. A retrospective statement of assumption kept apart from the election, as on the 海部 page; it gives no day for 就任, and under the packet rule a retrospective record is never a from.

claims.text: The same page says the election was held to choose a new president in place of 麻生総裁, who had stepped down (退陣した麻生総裁に代わる新たな総裁を選ぶため).

locator.section: first paragraph

claims.uncertainty: Retrospective party record written long after the event: a claim only, never a holder boundary; no structured date is stored. Prints 麻生総裁 (surname and title). The day he stepped down is not stated; never an until for 麻生太郎, and no end is inferred from the successor's election.

roles.scope_note: Two party election observations. The office is separate from prime minister; no national executive powers imported. CLAUDE-C01-18 extends the role to 1990-2009 with fourteen dated holder observations, placed before the 2024 and 2025 observations above, which are unchanged. A holder observation is dated by same-day party records naming the person as the (new) president after the result, or by his own Diet statement of the office; only 森喜朗 has a stated start (his own statement that he took office on 5 April 2000), and no holder has an end, because no source reviewed states the day a presidency ended. Party elections and selections, notices, candidacies, declarations and reports of results, index headlines, announced or prospective resignations, predecessor references (前総裁), continuation attestations and retrospective lists and histories are claims that never feed a holder; party rules are procedure only, never a date. Do not infer an outgoing president's last day from a successor's election, and never read the prime-ministership (jp_pm) into this office or the reverse.

roles.title: 内閣総理大臣 — Prime Minister of Japan

holder_claims.name: 海部俊樹
holder_claims.note: First appointment (10 August 1989 on the Kantei's retrospective page) lies before the period. Observed on 19 January 1990 signing the Cabinet's written answer No. 1 of the 117th session to the House of Councillors as 内閣総理大臣 海部俊樹: the earliest 1990 attestation pinned to a byte-stable response; the House of Representatives' answer of 23 January 1990 is a second. The acting Prime Minister's signature of 12 January 1990 (橋本龍太郎, 臨時代理) is a claim on the role, not this holder.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the appointment predates the period and no appointment instrument was reviewed, and no source states the day this appointment ended. The notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse and both Houses' designations of 27 February 1990 are claims on the role; the Kantei's span to 28 February 1990 is a retrospective claim only; the reappointment after the election is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: 海部俊樹
holder_claims.note: Observed on 2 March 1990, when he told both Houses in his policy speech that after the general election he had been appointed Prime Minister again (再び内閣総理大臣に任命され). Both Houses had designated him on 27 February 1990 (claims, never a start); he notified the Cabinet's resignation en masse as Prime Minister on 5 November 1991 (a claim).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the speeches give no date for the reappointment; the second cabinet's formation on 28 February 1990 rests only on retrospective claims (the Kantei page, the House of Councillors' table and a member's remark in debate), and no record of the 1990 Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day this appointment ended; the 5 November 1991 notice and 宮澤喜一's designation are not used as an end.

holder_claims.name: 宮澤喜一
holder_claims.note: Designated by both Houses on 5 November 1991 (claims); observed on 8 November 1991, when he told both Houses in his policy speech that he had now been appointed Prime Minister (このたび、私は、内閣総理大臣に任命され).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the 5 November 1991 formation rests on retrospective claims (the Kantei page, the House of Councillors' table and a minister's remark), and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the notice of his Cabinet's resignation en masse of 5 August 1993 and 細川護煕's designation are claims, and no source states that he continued to perform the duties until 9 August 1993.

holder_claims.name: 細川護煕
holder_claims.note: Designated by both Houses on 6 August 1993 (claims); observed on 23 August 1993, when he told both Houses in his first policy speech that he had now been appointed Prime Minister. A minister's and a member's later remarks that he gave an instruction as Prime Minister on 9 August and visited the Kagoshima disaster area on 13 August are claims dated by the day they recall, never holder dates. The House of Councillors' table and the Houses' written answers of August-September 1993 print 細川護熙 (熙); the Diet minutes and the Kantei print 細川護煕, the form used here.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the 9 August 1993 formation rests on retrospective claims and a minister's remark, and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the notice of his Cabinet's resignation en masse of 25 April 1994 and 羽田孜's designation are claims, and no record shows him performing the duties between 25 and 28 April 1994.

holder_claims.name: 羽田孜
holder_claims.note: Designated by both Houses on 25 April 1994 (claims); observed on 10 May 1994, when he told both Houses that he had been appointed Prime Minister (このたび、私は、内閣総理大臣に任命されました); the House of Representatives' record misprints the speaker label as 内目総理大臣.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: 28 April 1994 rests on the Kantei's retrospective list and a member's recollection (claims), and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the notice of his Cabinet's resignation en masse (decided 25 June 1994) and 村山富市's designation are claims, and no record shows him performing the duties between 25 and 30 June 1994.

holder_claims.name: 村山富市
holder_claims.note: Designated by both Houses on 29 June 1994 (the House of Representatives in a runoff; claims); observed on 18 July 1994, speaking as 内閣総理大臣 in his policy speech. Members referred to the 村山内閣 and to 村山総理 in committee on 6 July 1994; those references are claims and do not date this holder.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: 30 June 1994 rests only on his own recollection of 9 November 1994 and the Kantei's retrospective list (claims), and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the notice of his Cabinet's resignation en masse of 11 January 1996 and 橋本龍太郎's designation are claims.

holder_claims.name: 橋本龍太郎
holder_claims.note: From 11 January 1996: the Kantei's statement titled 橋本内閣総理大臣談話 and dated that day opens 'I have today taken on the heavy responsibility of Prime Minister' (私は、本日、内閣総理大臣の重責を担うことになりました); the capture's original Last-Modified is 17 January 1996. Both Houses designated him that day (claims), and the same page carries his instructions at that day's first cabinet meeting (a claim on the role).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day this appointment ended; the notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 7 November 1996 and his re-designation and new appointment that day are not used as this end. The start is day-only: the statement gives no hour and does not describe the appointment ceremony, of which no 1996 record was accessible. His own later recollections (8 November 1996 and 30 July 1998) are retrospective claims, not the basis of the start.

holder_claims.name: 橋本龍太郎
holder_claims.note: Observed on 8 November 1996, when 橋本総理 held the press conference after forming the second Hashimoto cabinet and set out its priorities 'as Prime Minister' (内閣総理大臣として). Both Houses re-designated him on 7 November 1996 (claims). The Kantei statement dated 7 November 1996 says the Prime Minister 'again' took on the office that day, but it prints no name, and its identity rests on the next day's press conference, so it is a claim on the role and not this holder's start.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: no same-day source that names him states the day of the November 1996 reappointment, and no record of the ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 30 July 1998, his statement of that day that he had decided to resign the office and 小渕恵三's designation are claims, not an end.

holder_claims.name: 小渕恵三
holder_claims.note: The House of Representatives designated him on 30 July 1998 and the House of Councillors designated 菅直人; the joint committee reached no agreement, and under Constitution art. 67(2) the Representatives' designation became the Diet's resolution (claims). Observed on 31 July 1998 in the Kantei's record headed 小渕内閣総理大臣記者会見録. His spoken remark there that 'today' he had come to bear responsibility as Prime Minister is contradicted by his statement in the same record that the new cabinet was launched the previous day, so it is not read as an assumption statement; the unnamed written statement of 31 July says 'on this occasion' (この度), with no day.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: 30 July 1998 rests on his next-day recollection, a dated photo caption and the Kantei's retrospective list (claims), and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended: the Cabinet judged on 4 April 2000 that he was 'lacking' under Constitution art. 70 and resigned en masse, and the acting Prime Minister and 森喜朗's appointment followed; none of these is used as an end.

holder_claims.name: 森喜朗
holder_claims.note: From 5 April 2000: the statement dated that day under the heading 森内閣総理大臣演説等 says he was appointed Prime Minister that day (本日、内閣総理大臣に任命され); the Kantei's account names 森喜朗 and says 森総理 was appointed at the Imperial appointment ceremony that night; the April 2000 cabinet list's profile gives 平成１２年４月５日内閣総理大臣. The Imperial Household Agency's schedule records a 親任式・認証官任命式 that day without naming the appointee (jp_kunaicho_ceremony_20000405, a claim on the role).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day this appointment ended; the notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 4 July 2000, his re-designation and his reappointment that night are not used as this end. The start is day-only; no clock time is stored.

holder_claims.name: 森喜朗
holder_claims.note: From 4 July 2000: the Kantei's account 第２次森内閣発足 says 森総理 was re-designated that afternoon and appointed at the Imperial appointment ceremony that night as the 86th Prime Minister. His statement of that day ('本日、再び内閣総理大臣の重責を担うことになりました') prints no name, and the Imperial Household Agency's schedule records the ceremony that day without naming the appointee; both are claims on the role.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day his office ended; the notices of the Cabinet's resignation en masse and his statement of 26 April 2001 that the Mori cabinet resigned that day, and 小泉純一郎's appointment that night, are not used as an end. The Kantei's span to 26 April 2001 is a retrospective claim.

holder_claims.name: 小泉純一郎
holder_claims.note: From 26 April 2001: the Kantei's account 小泉内閣発足 names 小泉純一郎, designated that afternoon, and says that night he attended (臨みました) the Prime Minister's appointment ceremony and the ministers' attestation at the Palace and then issued the Prime Minister's statement, which it quotes. That statement ('本日、内閣総理大臣に任命され') prints no name, and the Imperial Household Agency's schedule records the ceremony that day without naming the appointee; both are claims on the role.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day this appointment ended; the notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 19 November 2003 and his re-designation and reappointment that day are not used as this end. The account says he attended the ceremony rather than that he was appointed; the appointment itself is stated by the unnamed statement it quotes.

holder_claims.name: 小泉純一郎
holder_claims.note: From 19 November 2003: the Kantei's account 第二次小泉内閣の発足, dated that day, says 小泉総理 was re-designated and appointed at the Imperial appointment ceremony as the 88th Prime Minister, and his statement of that day (breadcrumb 小泉総理の演説・記者会見等) says he had again taken on the office that day. The Imperial Household Agency's schedule records the ceremony that day without naming the appointee (a claim on the role).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day this appointment ended; the notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 21 September 2005 and his reappointment that day are not used as this end. The account dates the ceremony through its date heading and the order of events (その後).

holder_claims.name: 小泉純一郎
holder_claims.note: From 21 September 2005: the Kantei's account 第３次小泉内閣の発足 says 小泉総理 was designated as the 89th Prime Minister and appointed at the Imperial appointment ceremony that day; his statement (breadcrumb 小泉総理の演説・記者会見等) says he had for the third time taken on the office that day; and the Imperial Household Agency's photo page for that day names the ceremony 親任式（小泉内閣総理大臣）. In office on 25 September 2006, when he gave the last interview of his term at the Prime Minister's Office.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no contemporaneous source states the day his office ended. The notices of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 26 September 2006, his statement that the Koizumi cabinet resigned that day, 安倍晋三's designation and appointment that night (this packet's closing boundary) and the Kantei's retrospective span to 26 September 2006 are claims, not an end; no source states that he continued to perform the duties until the successor's appointment.

holder_claims.name: 安倍晋三
holder_claims.note: From 26 September 2006: the Kantei statement titled 安倍内閣総理大臣談話 says he was appointed Prime Minister that day, the Kantei account dates the Imperial appointment ceremony (親任式) to that night, and the Imperial Household Agency's photo page captions 親任式（安倍内閣総理大臣）. These are the stacked 1990-2006 packet's closing-boundary responses, re-recorded here with rows that name him. In office on 24 September 2007 (press conference). Both Houses' designations of 26 September 2006 stay the stacked packet's claims.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source reviewed states the day this appointment ended. The resignation announcement of 12 September 2007, the 24 September remark that he would leave office 'tomorrow', the resignation en masse of 25 September 2007, 福田康夫's appointment on 26 September 2007 and the Kantei's retrospective span to 26 September 2007 are claims, never an end.

holder_claims.name: 福田康夫
holder_claims.note: From 26 September 2007: the Kantei account 福田内閣の発足 and the Chief Cabinet Secretary's press record date the Imperial appointment ceremony to the morning of that day (08:30), and the Imperial Household Agency's photo page captions 親任式（福田内閣総理大臣）. Designated on 25 September 2007 by the House of Representatives' resolution after the joint committee failed (the House of Councillors designated 小沢一郎); his press remark of 25 September (拝命) recalls the designation and is not a start.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source reviewed states the day this appointment ended. The resignation announcement of 1 September 2008, the unnamed statement of 24 September 2008 ('I have resigned', with no day), the resignation en masse and 麻生太郎's appointment that day, and the Kantei's retrospective span are claims, never an end.

holder_claims.name: 麻生太郎
holder_claims.note: From 24 September 2008: the Kantei account 麻生内閣の発足 dates the Imperial appointment ceremony to late that night (深夜), and the Imperial Household Agency's photo page captions 親任式（麻生内閣総理大臣）. Designated that day by the House of Representatives' resolution after the joint committee failed (the House of Councillors designated 小沢一郎).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source reviewed states the day this appointment ended. His statement of 16 September 2009 that he was leaving office gives no day; the resignation en masse and 鳩山由紀夫's appointment that day and the Kantei's retrospective span are claims, never an end.

holder_claims.name: 鳩山由紀夫
holder_claims.note: From 16 September 2009: the Kantei account 鳩山内閣の発足 dates the Imperial appointment ceremony to that night (the page names him as 鳩山総理), and the Imperial Household Agency's photo page captions 親任式（鳩山内閣総理大臣）. Both Houses designated him at the first ballot.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the sources conflict. His remarks at the last cabinet meeting of 4 June 2010 say that 'today' he leaves the post, and the Chief Cabinet Secretary gave the cabinet's span as running to 'today, 4 June'; but members' and the successor's statements of 15 June 2010 say the resigned cabinet continued its functions until the ceremony of 8 June, and the Kantei's retrospective span runs to 8 June. None is taken as an end.

holder_claims.name: 菅直人
holder_claims.note: From 8 June 2010: the Imperial Household Agency's photo page captions 親任式（菅内閣総理大臣）, and the Kantei account 菅内閣の発足 dates the ceremony to that night; in office on 11 June 2010 (policy speech). Both Houses designated him on 4 June 2010; his press remark of 8 June spoke of taking office that evening and is not a start.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source reviewed states the day this appointment ended. The resignation announcement of 26 August 2011, the resignation en masse of 30 August 2011, the continued performance of duties to 2 September 2011 (claims only), his departure from the Prime Minister's Office on 2 September, 野田佳彦's appointment and the Kantei's retrospective span are never an end.

holder_claims.name: 野田佳彦
holder_claims.note: From 2 September 2011: the Imperial Household Agency's photo page captions 親任式（野田内閣総理大臣）, the Kantei account dates the ceremony, and his press conference that day says he formally took office that day (本日…正式に内閣総理大臣に就任); in office on 13 September 2011. Designated on 30 August 2011 (the House of Councillors in a runoff).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source reviewed states the day this appointment ended. The resignation en masse and 安倍晋三's appointment on 26 December 2012, his departure from the Prime Minister's Office that day and the Kantei's retrospective span are claims, never an end.

holder_claims.name: 安倍晋三
holder_claims.note: From 26 December 2012: the Imperial Household Agency's photo page captions 親任式（安倍内閣総理大臣）, the Kantei account dates the ceremony, and his same-day statement and press conference say he received the appointment that day (本日…拝命); in office on 28 January 2013. Designated on 26 December 2012 (the House of Councillors in a runoff).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source reviewed states the day this appointment ended. The resignation en masse of 24 December 2014 and his re-designation and reappointment that day start a new holder observation and are not used as this end; the Kantei's retrospective span is a claim.

holder_claims.name: 安倍晋三
holder_claims.note: From 24 December 2014, after the general election: the Imperial Household Agency's photo page captions 親任式（安倍内閣総理大臣）, the Kantei account dates the ceremony, and his press conference that day says that from that day he continues to bear the office (本日…引き続き内閣総理大臣の重責を担う); in office on 12 February 2015. The second Abe cabinet had resigned that morning.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source reviewed states the day this appointment ended. The resignation en masse of 1 November 2017 and the reappointment that day start a new holder observation; the Kantei's retrospective span is a claim.

holder_claims.name: 安倍晋三
holder_claims.note: From 1 November 2017, after the general election: the Imperial Household Agency's photo page, the Kantei account and his same-day press conference (本日、第９８代内閣総理大臣として、引き続き…); in office on 17 November 2017. Until 16 September 2020: page 2 of the Official Gazette special extra issue No. 99 states that, 菅義偉 having been appointed on the 16th of that month, 安倍晋三, Prime Minister of the fourth Abe cabinet, lost his office.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is stated by the Official Gazette's notice of loss of office (内閣総理大臣及び国務大臣退官), not inferred from the successor's start. The resignation announcement of 28 August 2020, the resignation en masse and statement of 16 September 2020, his departure from the Prime Minister's Office and the Kantei's retrospective span are claims only.

holder_claims.name: 菅義偉
holder_claims.note: From 16 September 2020: page 2 of the Official Gazette No. 99 states he was appointed on the 16th of that month, the Kantei account dates the ceremony, the Imperial Household Agency's entry records 親任式（菅内閣総理大臣）, and the minutes of that night's first cabinet meeting, which he attended as Prime Minister, record his statement that he was appointed that day; in office that day (press conference). Until 4 October 2021: page 2 of the Official Gazette No. 83 states that he lost his office when 岸田文雄 was appointed on the 4th of that month.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is stated by the Official Gazette's notice of loss of office, not inferred from the successor's start. The resignation en masse of 4 October 2021, the Chief Cabinet Secretary's instruction that the outgoing cabinet respond to emergencies until the new cabinet was launched (a claim only) and the successor's designation are never an end by themselves.

holder_claims.name: 岸田文雄
holder_claims.note: From 4 October 2021: the Kantei account dates the ceremony, the Imperial Household Agency's entry records 親任式（岸田内閣総理大臣）, the Official Gazette No. 83 prints his appointment, and the minutes of that night's first cabinet meeting record his statement that he was appointed that day. Until 10 November 2021: page 2 of the Official Gazette No. 88 states that he, Prime Minister of the Kishida cabinet, lost his office when he was appointed again on the 10th of that month.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is stated by the Official Gazette, not inferred from his own reappointment. The resignation en masse under Constitution art. 70 that morning and the re-designation are claims only.

holder_claims.name: 岸田文雄
holder_claims.note: From 10 November 2021, after the general election: the Kantei account, the Imperial Household Agency's entry, the Official Gazette No. 88 and the minutes of that night's first cabinet meeting (本日，引き続き，内閣総理大臣の重責を担う). Until 1 October 2024: page 2 of the Official Gazette No. 45 states that he lost his office when 石破茂 was appointed on the 1st of that month.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is stated by the Official Gazette, not inferred from the successor's start. The resignation en masse of 1 October 2024 and the Chief Cabinet Secretary's instruction on emergencies until the new cabinet (a claim only) are never an end by themselves.

holder_claims.name: 石破茂
holder_claims.note: From 1 October 2024: the Official Gazette No. 45 prints his appointment, the Kantei account dates the ceremony (it prints 石破総理), the minutes of that night's first cabinet meeting name him in full with his statement that he was appointed that day, and he held a press conference as Prime Minister. The Imperial Household Agency's entry names no appointee. Until 11 November 2024: page 2 of the Official Gazette No. 52 states that he, Prime Minister of the first Ishiba cabinet, lost his office when he was appointed again on the 11th of that month.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is stated by the Official Gazette, not inferred from his own reappointment. The resignation en masse under Constitution art. 70 that morning and the re-designation are claims only. His LDP presidency is a separate party role that never feeds this one.

holder_claims.name: 石破茂
holder_claims.note: From 11 November 2024, after the general election: the Kantei account captured that day, the Official Gazette No. 52, the minutes of that night's first cabinet meeting (私は、本日、再び内閣総理大臣の重責を担う) and his press conference. Until 21 October 2025: page 2 of the Official Gazette No. 28 states that he, Prime Minister of the second Ishiba cabinet, lost his office when 高市早苗 was appointed on the 21st of that month.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is stated by the Official Gazette, not inferred from the successor's start. The resignation en masse of 21 October 2025 and the Chief Cabinet Secretary's instruction on emergencies until the new cabinet (a claim only) are never an end by themselves.

holder_claims.name: 高市早苗
holder_claims.note: From 21 October 2025: the Kantei account captured that day dates the ceremony, the Official Gazette No. 28 prints her appointment, the minutes of that night's first cabinet meeting name her with her statement that she was appointed that day, and her press conference says she was appointed the 104th Prime Minister. Until 18 February 2026: page 2 of the Official Gazette No. 9 states that she, Prime Minister of the first Takaichi cabinet, lost her office when she was appointed again on the 18th of that month.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is stated by the Official Gazette, not inferred from her own reappointment. The resignation en masse under Constitution art. 70 that morning and the re-designation are claims only. Her LDP presidency is a separate party role that never feeds this one.

holder_claims.name: 高市早苗
holder_claims.note: From 18 February 2026, after the general election: the Kantei account, the Official Gazette No. 9, the minutes of that night's first cabinet meeting (本日、再び内閣総理大臣の重責を担う) and her press conference. In office before the cutoff: listed as 内閣総理大臣 高市早苗君 at the House of Representatives Budget Committee's recess sitting of 27 July 2026, and shown as 高市総理 at the Kumamoto earthquake recovery headquarters on 4 September 2026.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: she holds this appointment at the 7 September 2026 cutoff, and no source states an end. A Kantei page dated after the cutoff is excluded.

roles.scope_note: 内閣総理大臣, the Prime Minister of Japan, head of government under the Constitution of Japan: designated by a resolution of the Diet (art. 67) and appointed by the Emperor (art. 6) at the Imperial appointment ceremony (親任式). CLAUDE-C01-12 keeps each House's designation vote, any joint committee and the House of Representatives' prevailing resolution, the Imperial appointment ceremony, the Prime Minister's same-day statements, a cabinet's formation, the notice of a cabinet's resignation en masse (総辞職), any continued performance of duties until a successor is appointed (art. 71) and an acting prime minister (臨時代理) as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where a same-day source that names the holder states the day of appointment or assumption of office (a Kantei statement or account, or the Imperial Household Agency's record of the ceremony), and an end only where a source states the day the office ended; no source reviewed does, so no holder has an end. Otherwise a holder is dated by attested_on, from a same-day act in office. A designation vote, a resignation en masse, a successor's designation or appointment and a cabinet's formation are never a boundary; continued performance of duties and acting service are recorded as claims, never as a separate holder of this role. Retrospective Kantei and House of Councillors lists and spans are claims with no structured date, and later recollections are never holder dates. Constitution texts establish procedure only, never a date. Ministers, deputy prime ministers, the Chief Cabinet Secretary acting as prime minister and party offices are outside this role; the LDP presidency is a separate party role. CLAUDE-C01-13 extends the role from 26 September 2006 to the cutoff under the same rules, adding the Official Gazette's appointment notices and the Cabinet's published minutes as same-day records of a start; its only ends are the days the Gazette's notices of loss of office (内閣総理大臣及び国務大臣退官) state for the appointments that ended from 2020 to 2026. A Kantei retrospective span, a resignation en masse or a successor's appointment is still never an end, and continued performance of duties and acting designations stay claims.

unresolved: Prime ministers 1990-2006 (CLAUDE-C01-12, JP-PM-01..10) are dated holder observations from the Diet minutes (the National Diet Library's minutes API), the Houses' written answers and precedents table, Kantei statements, accounts, agendas and press conferences (raw Internet Archive captures) and the Imperial Household Agency's schedules. Still open: the days of the Imperial appointment ceremonies of 1990-1998 (the Official Gazette 官報 for 1990-2006 is not available without restriction, and the Imperial Household Agency's website begins in late 1999); every end of office; any continued performance of duties under Constitution art. 71 after the resignations en masse of 1990-2006; the reason and span of the acting Prime Minister of 12 January 1990 and the end of 青木幹雄's acting service in April 2000; and the House of Representatives' own record of the 7 November 1996 resignation notice.

Stated starts: 橋本龍太郎 (11 January 1996), 森喜朗 (5 April and 4 July 2000) and 小泉純一郎 (26 April 2001, 19 November 2003 and 21 September 2005). No stated end. Every other holder is dated by attested_on: 海部俊樹 (19 January and 2 March 1990), 宮澤喜一 (8 November 1991), 細川護煕 (23 August 1993), 羽田孜 (10 May 1994), 村山富市 (18 July 1994), 橋本龍太郎 (8 November 1996) and 小渕恵三 (31 July 1998). Designation votes, resignations en masse, a successor's designation or appointment, cabinet formations and retrospective lists are not boundaries.
Acting prime ministers (橋本龍太郎 on 12 January 1990; 青木幹雄 from 09:00 on 3 April 2000) are claims only, never holders. Clock times are not stored.
Holders from 26 September 2006 to the 7 September 2026 cutoff (安倍晋三's first appointment onward) are outside this packet; 安倍晋三's appointment is recorded only as the closing-boundary claim.

Prime ministers 2006-2026 (CLAUDE-C01-13, JP-PM06-01..10) extend the role from 安倍晋三's appointment of 26 September 2006 to the cutoff with sixteen holder observations, from the Diet minutes API, Kantei statements, accounts, press conferences and the Chief Cabinet Secretary's press records (raw Internet Archive captures), the Cabinet's published meeting minutes, the Imperial Household Agency's schedules and photo pages, and the Official Gazette's special extra issues of 2020-2026. Every one of the sixteen has a stated start. Stated ends come only from the Official Gazette's notices of loss of office (内閣総理大臣及び国務大臣退官): 安倍晋三 (16 September 2020), 菅義偉 (4 October 2021), 岸田文雄 (10 November 2021 and 1 October 2024), 石破茂 (11 November 2024 and 21 October 2025) and 高市早苗 (18 February 2026); 高市早苗 holds her second appointment at the cutoff.

Still open for 2006-2026: the Official Gazette of 2006-2017, which is not available without restriction, and so every end of office from 安倍晋三's first appointment to his third; the conflict over the end of 鳩山由紀夫's office (his 'today' of 4 June 2010 and the Chief Cabinet Secretary's span to 4 June, against the statements of continued duties until the ceremony of 8 June); the House of Representatives' own record of the Aso cabinet's resignation notice of 16 September 2009; and the Kantei's 歴代内閣 pages 099-105, not reviewed.

Continued performance of duties after a resignation en masse is recorded only as claims (4-8 June 2010 and 30 August-2 September 2011, and the prospective emergency arrangements of 2008, 2010, 2021, 2024 and 2025), never as a holder or an end; the Cabinet Act art. 9 orders of acting ministers of 2007 and 2008 and the statement that no acting Prime Minister was designated in September 2007 are claims only. The 2006 appointment records are re-recorded from the 1990-2006 packet's closing-boundary responses under new source ids so that their rows can name the holder; the integrator may instead amend that packet's rows.
